A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 19-page LBM paper, including readable equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F. Pages 2–19 have identical text and rendered appearance; page 1 differs only in affiliation and arXiv version metadata.

before.justification: v1 reports original LBM tracking evaluations in Tables 1–4, ablations in Section 4.3 and Appendix C, and zebrafish trajectory analysis in Section 4.6.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original tracking evaluations, ablations, supplementary experiments, and zebrafish trajectory analysis.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain identical collision–streaming architecture, prediction and update procedures, training losses, and pixel-based object association.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Kubric training and evaluations on TAP-Vid DAVIS/Kinetics, RoboTAP, TAO, BFT, and OVT-B. The deformable-object and AnimalTrack subset evaluations and zebrafish application are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding main and appendix experiments. This includes Track-On and CoTracker3 in Figure 12 and SORT, ByteTrack, and OC-SORT in Table 9.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix B retain the same training budgets, dataset splits, input resolution, metrics, and evaluation procedures. Subset comparisons and efficiency measurements also use unchanged settings.

E4.justification: The component, layer, encoder, query, neighbor-count, pixel-management, and similarity ablations in Section 4.3 and Appendix C are unchanged. Qualitative robustness analyses and failure cases in Section 4.5 and Appendices D–E are also identical.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including Figure 12's error bars and Section 4.2's significance wording. No run-count, seed, or statistical-procedure information is added or removed.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are identical, including Tables 1–9 and appendix figures. For example, LBM retains 65.1 AJ on TAP-Vid DAVIS in Table 1 and 74.5 OWTA on BFT in Table 4.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8) and the accompanying mathematical definitions and reasoning are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient online tracking, collision–streaming modeling, tracking performance, and robustness for dynamic objects.

C2.justification: Result interpretations remain identical. Section 5 and Appendices E–F retain the same limitations, proposed remedies, and societal-impact discussion, including locality, background interference, and object-level recovery limitations.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B retain identical architecture specifications, optimizer settings, preprocessing, hardware, and training-time disclosures. The project-page link and Section 4.4's deployment and quantization details are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography are identical, preserving the cited works and positioning relative to prior point-tracking and open-world object-tracking methods.

P1.justification: Page 1 changes affiliation 2 from 'Institute of Zoology, CAS' to 'Kunming Institute of Zoology, CAS' and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Body prose, section ordering, and appendix text are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–16, Tables 1–9, captions, and page arrangement are unchanged. The first-page affiliation and version-stamp text edits preserve the existing layout structure.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the institutional affiliation more specific and updates version metadata. The scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and substantive presentation—including all appendices—are identical, establishing no meaningful change in overall paper quality.
